newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Burma leader arrives in Cambodia, visit meets protest.
newsitem.headline: Burma leader arrives in Cambodia, visit meets protest.

text.p: Burmese leader General Than Shwe arrived in Phnom Penh on Wednesday shortly after a protest against his visit was held in the city's centre.
Than Shwe, whose 44-member entourage also included powerful military chief Khin Nyunt, was greeted by King Norodom Sihanouk and co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen at the airport.
Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy earlier led a protest march in the capital against Burma's military rulers and in support of Burmese dissident Aung San Suu Kyi.
Witnesses said police fired two shots into the air near the U.S. Embassy in a confused effort to stop the march, and arrested two of Sam Rainsy's bodyguards.
Witnesses said no one was hurt in the incident.
The protesters, estimated at around 100, carried placards reading "Aung San Suu Kyi is a model for Asia," and "Long live the NLD" -- a reference to Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy party.
Sam Rainsy, who met Suu Kyi in Rangoon in August, heads the Khmer Nation Party (KNP), which is not recognised by the Phnom Penh government.
Sam Rainsy entered the embassy to deliver a statement to U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Quin explaining the purpose of the march and asking for support, witnesses said.

The protesters had eluded heavy police deployments throughout the city aimed at blocking the march. Authorities had sealed off the KNP headquarters with scores of police, barricades and a waste truck shortly before Than Shwe's arrival.
The protesters notified the Interior Ministry of their plans earlier this week but municipal authorities, citing security, said on Tuesday they would not allow the march.
The Rangoon government recently barred Suu Kyi, a Nobel Peace laureate, from giving regular weekend speeches at her home and blocked a congress planned for her party.
It also arrested hundreds of party activists and later released them in stages.

Than Shwe's four-day visit is his first to Cambodia since diplomatic ties were restored in 1994, officials said. Ranariddh paid an official visit to Burma in January. The two countries have signed a bilateral cooperation agreement.
Burmese transport ministry officials told Reuters the leaders of the two countries were expected to discuss air links.
